text: Later work by Gul Agha, starting with his book Actors (1986), made the model precise; in "A Foundation for Actor Computation" (Agha, Mason, Smith and Talcott, 1997) it comes down to three primitives an actor may use in response to a message: send messages to actors whose addresses it knows, create new actors, and become, choosing the behaviour for its next message.

title: Actors: A Model of Concurrent Computation in Distributed Systems (MIT Press, 1986); A foundation for actor computation (J. Functional Programming 7(1):1-72, 1997)

evidence: 1997: "The actor primitives are send, become and letactor: • send is for sending messages ... • letactor is for actor creation ... • become is for changing behavior" / Book page: "By Gul Agha, The MIT Press, DOI: https://doi.org/10.7551/mitpress/1086.001.0001, Publication date: 1986"
